context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud, providing sub-50ms decisions and case management for analysts. It ensures compliance, auditability, and high availability while operating within strict budget and team constraints.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Payers, Fraud Analysts, and Risk Managers/Quants.
- **External Systems**: Payment Gateway/Acquirer, Core Banking/Card Network Systems, Identity Provider (IdP).
- **Core Containers**: Edge Envoy Proxy on Amazon ECS Fargate, Real-Time Scoring Engine, Case Management Application, Audit and Storage Service.
- **Infrastructure**: Dedicated AWS VPC, Amazon S3 Glacier Vault Lock (WORM storage).

## Relationships
- **Payment Gateway to Edge Proxy**: HTTPS/gRPC via mTLS (TLS 1.3) for real-time transaction screening (R-01).
- **Users to IdP**: HTTPS using OAuth2/OIDC for authentication and RBAC.
- **Scoring Engine to Audit Storage**: AWS KMS encryption and Amazon S3 Object Lock for tamper-evident logs (R-06).

## Technology Stack
- **Compute/Edge**: Amazon ECS Fargate running Envoy proxy for perimeter mTLS termination, local caching, and fail-open timeout enforcement.
- **Security & Identity**: AWS IAM, Cognito, and AWS KMS customer-managed keys for tokenization and encryption.
- **Audit & Logging**: Amazon S3 Glacier Vault Lock for 7-year tamper-evident WORM storage.
- **Observability**: AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry with CloudWatch and X-Ray.
- **CI/CD**: GitHub Actions for automated blue/green deployments with cryptographically signed model artifacts.

## Rationale
AWS managed services and containerized Envoy proxies minimize operational toil for a three-person team while satisfying strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. Tiered storage and efficient edge routing meet the 3,000 TPS performance and 7-year audit constraints within the €25,000 monthly budget.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
This system provides real-time payment fraud screening and case management for card-not-present transactions, ensuring sub-50ms latency and strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. It enables fraud analysts to review suspicious payments while maintaining an immutable, tamper-evident audit trail for 7 years.

## Key Elements
* Payers, Fraud Analysts, and Risk Managers/Quants (Users)
* Payment Gateway/Acquirer, Core Banking/Card Network Systems, and Identity Provider (External Systems)
* AWS API Gateway / ALB (Ingress)
* Real-Time Scoring Engine (Containerized microservice on Amazon EC2 with auto-scaling)
* Case Management Backend (ECS Fargate service built with Node.js/TypeScript)
* Case Management UI (React Single-Page App hosted in Amazon S3 via CloudFront)
* Data & State: Redis (ElastiCache), PostgreSQL (RDS), and Amazon S3 with KMS and Object Lock
* Messaging & Security: Amazon SQS/EventBridge, AWS Secrets Manager, and AWS App Mesh / Istio

## Relationships
* Payers interact with the Payment Gateway, which forwards authorization requests via HTTPS/gRPC to AWS API Gateway.
* AWS API Gateway communicates with the Real-Time Scoring Engine over mTLS, utilizing a local fallback circuit breaker for availability.
* Real-Time Scoring Engine performs sub-millisecond feature lookups against Redis (ElastiCache).
* Fraud Analysts access the Case Management UI (CloudFront/S3), which communicates with the Case Management Backend (ECS Fargate) via HTTPS/OAuth2/OIDC.
* Case Management Backend reads/writes transactional case data to PostgreSQL (RDS).
* Scoring decisions, model versions, explanations, and analyst overrides are streamed via Amazon SQS/EventBridge and stored in Amazon S3 with Object Lock for 7-year auditability.

## Technology Stack
* Real-Time Scoring Engine: Go or Rust on Amazon EC2 for predictable memory and P99 latency < 50ms.
* Case Management Backend: Node.js/TypeScript on AWS ECS Fargate for rapid analyst tooling.
* Frontend: React hosted on Amazon S3 and delivered via Amazon CloudFront.
* Database & Caching: Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL) with row-level encryption and Amazon ElastiCache (Redis).
* Storage & Compliance: Amazon S3 with KMS and Object Lock (compliance mode) for 7-year audit retention.
* Networking & Security: AWS API Gateway/ALB, AWS App Mesh/Istio for mTLS, and AWS Secrets Manager.
* Deployment & Observability: AWS CodeDeploy (blue/green deployments), AWS CloudWatch, Prometheus, and Grafana.

## Rationale
This architecture isolates the high-throughput scoring engine on EC2 to guarantee sub-50ms P99 latencies under high transaction volume. Serverless and managed AWS components minimize operational overhead to fit a 3-person engineering team and a 25,000 EUR monthly budget while satisfying stringent PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability requirements.

AWS API Gateway / ALB.analysis:
## Overview
The system provides real-time payment fraud screening for a mid-size payment processor and case management for fraud analysts. It ingests and evaluates authorization requests while maintaining strict compliance, performance, and budget constraints.

## Key Elements
- Payers and Fraud Analysts (Users)
- Payment Gateway/Acquirer and Identity Provider (External Systems)
- AWS API Gateway / ALB (Ingress Layer)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Amazon EC2, Go/Rust)
- Case Management Backend (AWS ECS Fargate, Node.js/TypeScript)
- Case Management UI (Amazon S3, Amazon CloudFront, React)
- Redis Cache (Amazon ElastiCache)
- PostgreSQL Database (Amazon RDS)
- Audit Storage (Amazon S3 with KMS and Object Lock)
- Messaging Bus (Amazon SQS / EventBridge)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway/Acquirer -> AWS API Gateway / ALB: Forwards authorization requests [HTTPS/gRPC]
- AWS API Gateway / ALB -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Communicates scoring requests using local circuit breaker [mTLS]
- Case Management UI -> AWS API Gateway / ALB: Sends management and review traffic [HTTPS]
- AWS API Gateway / ALB -> Case Management Backend: Routes administrative and review APIs [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ALB: Handles high-throughput payment ingestion for sub-50ms latency.
- AWS API Gateway: Manages case management APIs and IdP integrations.
- Amazon EC2: Hosts the real-time scoring engine for optimal CPU performance.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Runs containerized case management backend with low operational overhead.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Stores tamper-evident audit logs to meet 7-year compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services to minimize maintenance overhead for a three-engineer team within a strict 25,000 EUR monthly budget. The split ingress topology separates high-throughput payment traffic from management APIs to guarantee sub-50ms P99 latency and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

Real-Time Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud under 50 milliseconds while providing case management tools for fraud analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS compliance, 7-year tamper-evident auditability, and 99.99% availability within a strict monthly infrastructure budget.

## Key Elements
* AWS API Gateway / ALB
* Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go, AWS ECS Fargate)
  * API Handler Component (Go net/http)
  * Feature Aggregator Component
  * In-Memory Scoring Engine Component (with WASM models and Explainability Formatter)
  * Audit Publisher Component
  * Circuit Breaker Fallback Controller
* Case Management Backend (Node.js, TypeScript, AWS ECS Fargate)
* Case Management UI (React, Amazon S3, Amazon CloudFront)
* Redis Cache (Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) with TLS 1.3)
* Audit Storage (Amazon S3 with KMS envelope encryption and Object Lock)
* Messaging Bus (Amazon SQS / EventBridge)

## Relationships
* AWS API Gateway / ALB -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Forwards authorization requests using mTLS with a local circuit breaker [mTLS]
* Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Redis Cache: Performs sub-millisecond feature lookups [Redis Protocol over TLS 1.3]
* Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Messaging Bus: Streams tamper-evident logs and telemetry [Amazon SQS / AMQP]
* Audit Publisher -> Audit Storage: Writes cryptographically signed, encrypted decision logs [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
* Case Management Backend -> PostgreSQL Database: Manages review cases and analyst workflows [PostgreSQL Protocol]

## Technology Stack
* Go: Selected for the Real-Time Scoring Engine to guarantee P99 latency below 50 ms at 3,000 TPS with minimal garbage collection overhead.
* AWS ECS Fargate: Provides container orchestration without the operational toil of bare EC2 and avoids cold-start latency risks of serverless functions.
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Delivers sub-millisecond feature caching for real-time behavioral profiling.
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock and KMS: Ensures tamper-evident, encrypted 7-year audit storage compliant with R-06.
* React & Node.js (TypeScript): Powers the Case Management UI and Backend for efficient analyst case review workflows.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages containerized Go microservices on AWS ECS Fargate to strictly satisfy the sub-50ms P99 latency and high-throughput requirements within a 3-engineer team constraint. Security and compliance controls—such as tokenized payload stripping, local cryptographic signing, and S3 Object Lock—ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability while staying safely within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Case Management Backend.analysis:
## Overview
[The Case Management Backend is a Node.js and TypeScript container running on AWS ECS Fargate that processes fraud analyst reviews and audit logs for the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system. It enforces strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability while staying within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]

## Key Elements
- API Router / Controller (TypeScript, Express/Fastify)
- Case Workflow Service (TypeScript)
- Audit & Compliance Logger (TypeScript)
- Messaging Consumer/Publisher (TypeScript)
- Masking & Sanitization Middleware (TypeScript)
- PostgreSQL Database (Amazon RDS PostgreSQL)
- Audit Storage (Amazon S3 with Object Lock)
- Messaging Bus (Amazon SQS / EventBridge)

## Relationships
- API Router -> Case Workflow Service: Invokes business logic [Internal Function Call]
- API Router -> Masking & Sanitization Middleware: Sanitizes payloads [Internal Function Call]
- Case Workflow Service -> Audit & Compliance Logger: Triggers immutable logging [Internal Function Call]
- Case Workflow Service -> PostgreSQL Database: Persists case state [TypeORM/Prisma via PostgreSQL Protocol]
- Audit & Compliance Logger -> Audit Storage (Amazon S3): Writes cryptographically signed audit logs [HTTPS/S3 API]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js & TypeScript: Enables rapid iteration and workflow logic within a three-engineer team constraint
- AWS ECS Fargate: Provides container orchestration while maintaining a single tightly controlled security perimeter
- Amazon RDS PostgreSQL: Persists transactional case data securely with AWS KMS-managed encryption at rest
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Stores tamper-evident, cryptographically signed audit logs for 7-year regulatory compliance
- AWS Secrets Manager: Manages database credentials with automated rotation directly in ECS task definitions

## Rationale
[This architecture unifies core backend logic within AWS ECS Fargate to satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 boundaries and simplify IAM enforcement. Asynchronous audit logging and in-memory buffering ensure sub-second analyst UX while meeting strict auditability requirements.]

Case Management UI.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management UI is a secure, serverless Single-Page Application enabling fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions and risk managers to manage rules. It operates within AWS eu-west-1, strictly enforcing PCI-DSS compliance and auditability requirements.

## Key Elements
- **Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers**: Primary system users accessing the interface
- **Auth & Router Component**: React Router and `oidc-client-ts` managing PKCE authentication and RBAC
- **Case Queue & Investigation Component**: React and TanStack Query handling masked card data and review queues
- **Rule Management & Audit Component**: React, Formik, Zod, and Recharts for rule staging and metrics
- **Amazon S3 & CloudFront**: Static asset hosting and global content delivery
- **Case Management Backend**: Upstream API service communicating via HTTPS

## Relationships
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management UI: Accesses investigation queues [HTTPS via TLS 1.3]
- Risk Managers -> Case Management UI: Manages rules and views metrics [HTTPS via TLS 1.3]
- Case Management UI -> Amazon CloudFront: Delivers static SPA assets [HTTPS]
- Case Management UI -> Case Management Backend: Submits API requests [HTTPS/REST, OAuth2/OIDC]

## Technology Stack
- **React & TypeScript**: Frontend framework for component-based UI development
- **Amazon S3 & CloudFront**: Serverless static hosting ensuring zero OS-level maintenance for a 3-engineer team
- **TanStack Query (React Query)**: State management for API polling and data synchronization
- **OIDC Client (`oidc-client-ts`)**: Secure PKCE token exchange handling

## Rationale
The serverless React/S3/CloudFront stack minimizes operational overhead to fit the 3-engineer constraint while maintaining the €25,000 monthly budget. Client-side security controls and TLS 1.3 enforce strict PCI-DSS compliance and data protection.

Redis Cache.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations and manages reviews for fraud analysts. The architecture uses low-latency caching to meet rigorous performance and security constraints.

## Key Elements
- In-Memory Data Store (Redis Engine)
- Persistence/Backup Worker (AWS ElastiCache Managed Snapshot)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Redis Cache: Performs sub-millisecond feature lookups using RESP over TCP with mTLS and TLS 1.3
- Redis Cache -> Amazon S3: Stores daily automated backups with a 7-day retention period

## Technology Stack
- Amazon ElastiCache for Redis (Cluster Mode Disabled, Multi-AZ): Selected for sub-millisecond performance to meet the P99 < 50ms latency requirement.
- Graviton2 cache.m6g.large instances: Chosen for optimal price-performance to adhere to the €25,000/month infrastructure budget.
- Redis 7.x native ACLs and AWS IAM Database Authentication: Implemented to enforce least-privilege access and PCI-DSS compliance.
- AWS KMS: Used for at-rest encryption of cached cryptographic tokens and feature sets.

## Rationale
This architecture achieves sub-millisecond state lookups required for high-throughput fraud scoring while strictly containing costs for a three-person engineering team. It maintains PCI-DSS compliance through robust encryption, strict data minimization, and isolated private subnet deployment.

PostgreSQL Database.analysis:
## Overview
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluating card-not-present payment authorizations and managing fraud analyst reviews.
- Built for a mid-size payment processor under strict PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability constraints.

## Key Elements
- **Case Repository Component**: Manages CRUD operations and state transitions for investigator reviews.
- **Audit & Compliance Log Component**: Handles append-only decision logs and analyst override histories using partitioned tables.
- **Database Security Manager**: Enforces AWS KMS-backed encryption and PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS).
- **Primary RDS Instance**: Handles transactional case state updates.
- **Read Replica**: Dedicated to analyst reporting, audit queries, and read-heavy analytics.
- **PgBouncer**: Connection pooler hosted alongside the Case Management Backend.

## Relationships
- **Case Management Backend -> Primary RDS Instance**: Executes transactional writes and state updates via [PostgreSQL Protocol / TLS 1.3].
- **Case Management Backend -> Read Replica**: Routes read-heavy analytics and case history queries via [PostgreSQL Protocol / TLS 1.3].
- **PostgreSQL Database -> Amazon CloudWatch / S3 Object Lock**: Streams audit logs using `pgaudit` via [AWS API / HTTPS].

## Technology Stack
- **Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL)**: Core database chosen for native partitioning, RLS, and strict compliance support.
- **AWS KMS**: Provides customer-managed keys (CMK) for Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) to satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1.
- **PgBouncer**: Manages database connection spikes to prevent thread exhaustion during traffic surges.
- **`pgaudit` Extension**: Logs DDL, DCL, and role changes for tamper-evident 7-year audit trails.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Delivers automated 30-day rotation for short-lived database credentials.

## Rationale
- Partitioned tables and dedicated read replicas optimize performance for high-throughput transactional writes and 7-year historical audit scans.
- Native PostgreSQL security controls and managed AWS services minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while ensuring compliance.

Audit Storage.analysis:
## Overview
This system provides real-time payment fraud screening for card-not-present authorizations, returning approve, decline, or review decisions. It features case management for analysts, strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a fixed AWS budget.

## Key Elements
- **Payers & Fraud Analysts**: End users submitting payments and reviewing flagged transactions.
- **AWS API Gateway / ALB**: Ingress routing and load balancing.
- **Real-Time Scoring Engine**: Go/Rust container on Amazon EC2 evaluating fraud rules.
- **Case Management Backend & UI**: Node.js/TypeScript on AWS ECS Fargate and React on S3/CloudFront.
- **Audit Storage**: Amazon S3 with KMS and Object Lock, backed by Amazon DynamoDB indexing.
- **Audit Sub-Components**: Audit Writer, Audit Query API, and Report Generator (Go, AWS Lambda).

## Relationships
- Payers -> AWS API Gateway / ALB: Submits authorization requests [HTTPS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Redis Cache: Retrieves rules and customer velocity data [Redis Protocol]
- Audit Writer -> Amazon S3: Persists immutable decision records [HTTPS / AWS SDK]
- Audit Query API -> Amazon DynamoDB: Queries indexed decision metadata [HTTPS]
- Report Generator -> Amazon S3 (Staging): Generates signed export packages [HTTPS / AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- **Compute**: Amazon EC2 (Scoring), AWS ECS Fargate (Case Management), AWS Lambda (Audit/Export APIs) for serverless scalability.
- **Storage/Database**: Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL) for transactional data, Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) for fast caching, Amazon S3 with KMS/Object Lock for immutable 7-year audit logs.
- **Infrastructure as Code**: Terraform / AWS CDK managed by a 3-engineer team within a 25,000 EUR/month budget.

## Rationale
The architecture combines low-latency EC2 scoring nodes with serverless AWS Lambda components to meet P99 performance targets under 50 ms. Leveraging managed AWS services (S3 Object Lock, DynamoDB, KMS) ensures PCI-DSS compliance and tamper-evident 7-year auditability while minimizing operational overhead for a three-engineer team.

Messaging Bus.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present transactions for a mid-size payment processor and provides a case management interface for fraud analysts.]

## Key Elements
* AWS API Gateway / ALB
* Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go/Rust on Amazon EC2)
* Case Management Backend (Node.js, TypeScript on Amazon ECS Fargate)
* Case Management UI (React on Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront)
* Redis Cache (Amazon ElastiCache)
* PostgreSQL Database (Amazon RDS)
* Audit Storage (Amazon S3 with KMS and Object Lock)
* Messaging Bus (Amazon SQS Standard, SQS FIFO, and Dead-Letter Queues)
* Audit Storage Worker (AWS Lambda)

## Relationships
* Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Scoring Event Queue: Publishes decision payloads via AWS SDK (HTTPS)
* Case Management Backend -> Audit Event Queue: Publishes analyst overrides via AWS SDK (HTTPS)
* Audit Event Queue -> Audit Storage Worker: Consumes message batches via Event Source Mapping (HTTPS)
* Audit Storage Worker -> Audit Storage: Writes tamper-evident logs via Amazon S3 API (HTTPS)
* Scoring Event Queue -> Analytics/Monitoring Consumer: Streams telemetry via AWS SDK (HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
* AWS SQS Standard & SQS FIFO: Selected for high-throughput messaging, guaranteed ordering, and at-least-once delivery.
* AWS Lambda: Chosen for serverless, event-driven consumption of SQS queues within a 3-engineer team capacity.
* AWS KMS: Utilized with customer-managed keys (CMKs) to encrypt SQS queues and satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.
* Amazon S3 Object Lock: Implemented to provide tamper-evident storage for 7-year audit requirements.
* AWS VPC Endpoints (PrivateLink): Enforced for secure internal communication, bypassing the public internet.

## Rationale
[This architecture guarantees high-throughput and sub-50ms P99 latency while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year tamper-evident audit trail. Furthermore, fully managed serverless AWS components keep operational overhead minimal for a three-engineer team within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]
